title: Your Life as a Gladiator at Every Level (Survive to Level 7)
hook: Sand in your teeth. Blood cooling on a stranger's blade. Sixty thousand throats gone silent, waiting on a thumb that hasn't turned yet. You're not free. You're property that just won a fight.
body: POV: a composite Roman gladiator who climbs the real, documented palus grading system inside a ludus (gladiator school) -- Novicius (bought at the auction block) to Tiro (your first bout) to Quartus and Secundus Palus (the win-ranked grades gladiators actually held, per weapon style) to Primus Palus (the champion tier) to a free man who earns the rudis, the real wooden sword of discharge, and refuses it -- to Lanista (you own the ludus) to the editor/emperor above even that, funding games at imperial scale. Real, verified mechanics woven in: the palus ranking tiers; the rudis threshold (roughly 30 fights or five years' service); Emperor Marcus Aurelius's actual 12,000-sestertii cap on what a lanista could charge to re-book a star fighter; the real munera cost tiers for booking a bill of gladiators; and Trajan's Dacian triumph games, reported at 123 days and roughly 10,000 gladiators across the run (a later secondary source, used here as order-of-magnitude scale, not an audited count). Flamma, the real gladiator who refused freedom four separate times, and Marcus Attilius's real documented upset of a seasoned imperial fighter both ground this story's shape. Priscus (the mentor doctore) and Barca (the rival) are a FICTIONAL COMPOSITE; no real historical figure is depicted as this episode's protagonist. Watch the whole series -- every life, every level, every level the crowd decides you don't get to walk away from. For educational and entertainment purposes.
pinned: Real fact: gladiators were nicknamed "hordearii" -- barley-men -- because their trainers fed them a mostly grain diet to build a layer of fat on purpose. Bioarchaeologists who studied gladiator bones confirmed it: the fat cushioned cuts and reduced visible blood loss for the crowd, without slowing footwork much. Which level do you think costs the most: the first bout, or the day the rudis gets refused?
poll: Which level costs the most? LEVEL 02 (the first bout -- a nobody, standing, alive) / LEVEL 05 (Primus Palus -- the editor learns your doctore's name) / LEVEL 06 (the rudis offered, handed back) / LEVEL 08 (the editor's box -- the top of the ladder still isn't safe)
